description: Comprehensive question bank on Social Change - Modernisation, Westernisation, Secularisation, Globalisation, Industrialisation, Urbanisation and Social Mobility. Based on FDA & SDA Examination Notes Chapter 5.3.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is social change?

options.A: Significant changes over time in the structure, institutions, relationships, values, norms, behaviour and patterns of life in a society

questions.explanation: Social change refers to significant changes over time in the structure, institutions, relationships, values, norms, behaviour and patterns of life in a society.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is modernisation?

options.A: A broad process through which societies undergo structural, technological, economic, political, educational and cultural transformation
options.B: Only the adoption of Western clothing

questions.explanation: Modernisation is a broad process involving structural, technological, economic, political, educational and cultural transformation, often involving scientific knowledge, industrial and service-sector growth, urbanisation, rational organisation and expanded institutional participation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Is modernisation identical to Westernisation?

options.A: Yes, they are the same process
options.B: No, modernisation refers to broad structural and institutional change, while Westernisation refers to adoption of Western cultural practices
options.C: Yes, both mean adopting Western culture
options.D: No, Westernisation is broader than modernisation

questions.explanation: Modernisation refers to broad structural and institutional change, while Westernisation refers to the adoption or influence of selected Western cultural practices, institutions, ideas and technologies. A society can modernise in ways shaped by its own history and culture.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a major feature of modernisation?

options.A: Scientific temper

questions.explanation: Major features of modernisation include scientific temper, technological development, industrial and service-sector expansion, urban growth, literacy and education, occupational specialisation, bureaucratic organisation, mass communication, mobility, individual achievement and wider political participation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following promotes modernisation?

options.A: Education and science

questions.explanation: Education, science and technology, industrial development, transport, communication, urbanisation, economic growth, democratic institutions, administrative reform, public health and interaction with other societies can promote modernisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of science and technology in modernisation?

options.A: They improve production, communication, transport, healthcare, agriculture, education and public administration
options.C: They have no role in modernisation

questions.explanation: Science and technology improve production, communication, transport, healthcare, agriculture, education and public administration. They can increase productivity and access to information, while also creating concerns such as unequal digital access, job displacement and privacy risks.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between modernisation and education?

options.A: Education spreads scientific knowledge, literacy, technical skills and critical thinking
options.B: Education has no relation to modernisation

questions.explanation: Education spreads scientific knowledge, literacy, technical skills, critical thinking and awareness of rights. It supports occupational change and enables people to participate in modern economic and political institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does modernisation automatically produce democracy?

options.A: Yes, modernisation always leads to democracy
options.B: No, democratic development also depends on institutions, rights, accountability and political choices
options.C: Yes, but only in Western countries

questions.explanation: Modernisation can expand education, communication, political awareness and participation, but it does not automatically produce democracy. Democratic development also depends on institutions, rights, accountability and political choices.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is rationalisation in the context of modernisation?

options.A: The increasing organisation of activities through calculation, systematic rules, evidence, efficiency and predictable procedures
options.C: Reliance only on custom and personal authority

questions.explanation: Rationalisation is the increasing organisation of activities through calculation, systematic rules, evidence, efficiency and predictable procedures rather than relying only on custom or personal authority.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is secular-rational thinking?

options.A: Explaining social and natural events through reason, evidence and publicly testable explanations

questions.explanation: Secular-rational thinking explains social and natural events through reason, evidence and publicly testable explanations rather than relying exclusively on supernatural explanations. It does not necessarily require individuals to abandon religious belief.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is tradition?

options.A: Inherited customs, beliefs and practices transmitted across generations

questions.explanation: Tradition refers to inherited customs, beliefs and practices transmitted across generations. Modernity is associated with newer social, economic, political and cultural arrangements such as scientific organisation, industrial economies and modern institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a positive effect of modernisation?

options.A: Higher productivity

questions.explanation: Potential positive effects include higher productivity, improved infrastructure, wider education, better healthcare, occupational opportunities, greater social mobility, improved communication and expanded access to public services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a negative effect of modernisation?

options.A: Environmental degradation

questions.explanation: Possible challenges include environmental degradation, consumerism, inequality, cultural dislocation, weakening of some traditional support networks, job displacement, digital exclusion and uneven distribution of development.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is meant by the uneven nature of modernisation?

options.A: Modernisation affects all groups equally
options.B: Modernisation does not affect all regions, classes, castes, genders or communities equally

questions.explanation: Modernisation does not affect all regions, classes, castes, genders or communities equally. Some groups gain access to technology, education and employment earlier than others, creating uneven development.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Indian sociologist is associated with the concept of the 'modernisation of Indian tradition'?

options.A: M. N. Srinivas

questions.explanation: Yogendra Singh is widely associated with the study of the modernisation of Indian tradition. He examined how modern institutions and processes interact with and transform traditional social structures in India.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the main argument of Yogendra Singh's approach to modernisation?

options.A: Modernisation means complete disappearance of tradition
options.B: Traditional institutions can change, adapt and sometimes gain new forms or functions under modern conditions

questions.explanation: Modernisation in India should not be understood simply as the disappearance of tradition. Traditional institutions can change, adapt and sometimes gain new forms or functions under modern conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which classical sociologist is associated with the analysis of rationalisation in modern society?

options.A: Max Weber

questions.explanation: Classical sociologists such as Emile Durkheim, Max Weber and Ferdinand Tonnies analysed major transitions associated with modern society, including division of labour, rationalisation and changing forms of social relationships.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which classical sociologist is associated with the analysis of division of labour in modern society?

options.A: Emile Durkheim

questions.explanation: Emile Durkheim analysed division of labour as a major transition associated with modern society.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is Westernisation?

options.A: The process through which a society adopts or is influenced by cultural practices, values, institutions and ideas associated with Western societies
options.B: The rejection of all foreign influence

questions.explanation: Westernisation is the process through which a society adopts or is influenced by cultural practices, values, institutions, technologies, education systems, lifestyles and ideas associated with Western societies.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Indian sociologist developed the concept of Westernisation in the study of Indian society?

options.A: Yogendra Singh

questions.explanation: M. N. Srinivas developed and used the concept of Westernisation to explain changes in Indian society under the influence of British rule and wider Western contact.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How did M. N. Srinivas explain Westernisation?

options.A: As changes in Indian society resulting from prolonged contact with Western, especially British, culture and institutions
options.B: As the complete rejection of Indian culture
options.C: As the same process as Sanskritisation

questions.explanation: M. N. Srinivas used Westernisation to describe changes in Indian society resulting from prolonged contact with Western, especially British, culture and institutions. These changes included technology, education, institutions, ideology and values.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following areas was influenced by Westernisation in India?

options.A: Modern education

questions.explanation: Major areas include modern education, English-language use, law and administration, scientific and technological knowledge, transport, communication, clothing, food habits, architecture, political ideas and some social reform movements.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What role did British rule play in Westernisation in India?

options.A: It introduced Western-style administrative, legal and educational institutions, railways, postal and telegraph systems
options.B: It had no impact on Indian society

questions.explanation: British rule introduced or expanded Western-style administrative, legal and educational institutions, railways, postal and telegraph systems, modern military and bureaucratic structures, and English-language education. These changes also served colonial interests and were not simply acts of social progress.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How did Western education influence Indian society?

options.A: It contributed to the spread of modern sciences, new forms of professional training and political ideas
options.C: It had no impact on Indian society
options.D: It was equally accessible to all sections of society

questions.explanation: Western education contributed to the spread of modern sciences, new forms of professional training, political ideas, liberal and constitutional thought, print culture and reform debates. Access was unequal and closely shaped by colonial policies and social conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How did Westernisation influence Indian social reform?

options.A: It contributed to debates and movements concerning sati, child marriage, caste discrimination, women's education and widow remarriage
options.B: It had no impact on social reform

questions.explanation: Exposure to new ideas and institutions contributed to debates and movements concerning practices such as sati, child marriage, caste discrimination, women's education and widow remarriage. Indian reformers interpreted and adapted ideas in their own social and historical contexts.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between Westernisation and modernisation?

options.A: Westernisation refers to influence or adoption of Western-origin practices and institutions, while modernisation refers to wider structural change
options.C: Modernisation refers only to Western influence

questions.explanation: Westernisation refers to influence or adoption of Western-origin practices and institutions. Modernisation refers to wider structural change involving technology, economy, education, administration and social organisation; modernisation need not mean copying the West.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between Westernisation and Sanskritisation?

options.A: Westernisation refers to changes associated with contact with Western culture, while Sanskritisation refers to a lower-status caste adopting practices of a higher-status group

questions.explanation: Westernisation, in M. N. Srinivas's usage, refers to changes associated with contact with Western culture and institutions. Sanskritisation refers to a process in which a lower-status caste or group adopts practices and customs associated with a locally influential or higher-status group.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does Westernisation mean the complete rejection of Indian culture?

options.A: Yes, Westernisation means complete rejection of Indian culture
options.B: No, Westernisation may involve selective adoption, adaptation or rejection of particular practices
options.C: Yes, Indian culture was completely destroyed
options.D: No, Westernisation had no impact on Indian culture

questions.explanation: Westernisation may involve selective adoption, adaptation or rejection of particular practices. Indian society has combined Western influences with indigenous traditions and institutions in varied ways.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a positive consequence of Westernisation?

options.A: Wider modern education

questions.explanation: Potential consequences include wider modern education, scientific and technological learning, constitutional and democratic ideas, professional institutions, new forms of public debate and reform movements.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a criticism of Westernisation?

options.A: Cultural imitation without critical assessment

questions.explanation: Criticisms include cultural imitation without critical assessment, consumerism, cultural domination, weakening of some local practices and the colonial context in which many Western institutions were introduced.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is cultural diffusion?

options.A: The spread of cultural traits, ideas, technologies or practices from one society or group to another
options.B: The rejection of all foreign culture

questions.explanation: Cultural diffusion is the spread of cultural traits, ideas, technologies or practices from one society or group to another through contact, migration, trade, media, education or conquest.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can Westernisation occur without colonial rule?

options.A: No, Westernisation requires colonial rule
options.B: Yes, Western cultural influences can spread through trade, migration, education, media, technology, diplomacy and global economic relations
options.C: No, Westernisation is only possible through conquest
options.D: Yes, but only through military occupation

questions.explanation: Yes. Western cultural influences can spread through trade, migration, education, media, technology, diplomacy and global economic relations even without direct colonial rule.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the significance of English education in colonial India?

options.A: It helped create new professional and administrative groups and facilitated access to Western literature, science and political ideas
options.B: It had no impact on Indian society
options.D: It was equally accessible to all sections of society

questions.explanation: English education helped create new professional and administrative groups and facilitated access to Western literature, science and political ideas. Its expansion was also linked to colonial administrative and economic objectives.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is secularisation?

options.A: A process in which social institutions, public authority, law, education or other areas of social life become less directly controlled by religious institutions
options.C: The establishment of a state religion

questions.explanation: Secularisation is a process in which social institutions, public authority, law, education or other areas of social life become less directly controlled by religious institutions or religious explanations. Its extent and form vary across societies.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between secularisation and secularism?

options.A: Secularisation is a social process involving changes in the influence of religion, while secularism is a political or constitutional principle

questions.explanation: Secularisation is a social process involving changes in the influence and role of religion. Secularism is a political or constitutional principle concerning the relationship between the State, religion and equal citizenship.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major dimensions of secularisation?

options.A: Differentiation of secular institutions from religious institutions
options.B: Declining or changing religious authority in some areas
options.C: Reduction of religious control over certain public decisions

questions.explanation: Commonly discussed dimensions include differentiation of secular institutions from religious institutions, declining or changing religious authority in some areas, and the reduction of religious control over certain public decisions. These dimensions do not necessarily occur together or at the same pace.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is institutional differentiation in secularisation?

options.A: The process through which institutions such as government, law, education, science and the economy develop their own specialised functions
options.B: The merging of religious and secular institutions
options.C: The establishment of a state religion

questions.explanation: Institutional differentiation is the process through which institutions such as government, law, education, science and the economy develop their own specialised functions rather than being directly governed by religious authorities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does secularisation necessarily mean the disappearance of religion?

options.A: Yes, secularisation means religion completely disappears
options.B: No, religion may remain important in personal life, community identity, public debate and politics
options.D: No, secularisation has no effect on religion

questions.explanation: No. Religion may remain important in personal life, community identity, public debate and politics even when some institutions become more independent of religious authority.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does secularism mean in the Indian Constitution?

options.A: India has no official State religion and the State must operate consistently with constitutional guarantees of equality, freedom of conscience and religious freedom
options.B: India has an official State religion
options.C: The State completely separates from religion in all matters
options.D: The State promotes one particular religion

questions.explanation: Indian secularism means that India has no official State religion and that the State must operate consistently with constitutional guarantees of equality, freedom of conscience and religious freedom. The State may regulate secular activities associated with religion and undertake social reform within constitutional limits.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment was the word 'secular' inserted into the Preamble?

options.A: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976

questions.explanation: The word 'secular' was inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, along with the word 'socialist'.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Did religious freedom exist in the Constitution before the 42nd Amendment?

options.A: No, religious freedom was introduced only by the 42nd Amendment
options.B: Yes, the original Constitution already contained important protections for freedom of conscience and religion
options.C: No, religious freedom was introduced by the 44th Amendment
options.D: Yes, but only for minority communities

questions.explanation: Yes. The original Constitution already contained important protections for freedom of conscience and religion, including Articles 25 to 28, as well as equality and minority cultural and educational rights.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with freedom of religion?

options.A: Articles 14 to 18

questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 deal with freedom of conscience, the right to profess, practise and propagate religion, management of religious affairs, taxation for promotion of religion and religious instruction in educational institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 25 guarantee?

options.A: Freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion

questions.explanation: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 26 guarantee?

options.A: Rights of religious denominations to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage religious affairs, and own and administer property
options.D: Right to life and personal liberty

questions.explanation: Article 26 protects the rights of religious denominations or sections thereof to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage religious affairs, and own and administer property in accordance with law, subject to public order, morality and health.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 27 provide?

options.A: Protection from being compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion of any particular religion
options.D: Right against religious instruction in educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 27 protects persons from being compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 28 provide?

options.A: Regulation of religious instruction or worship in educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 28 regulates religious instruction or worship in educational institutions and provides protections concerning participation or attendance in specified circumstances.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between Indian secularism and strict separation of religion and State?

options.A: Indian secularism is not always described as an absolute wall of separation; the State may engage with religious institutions for reform and regulation within constitutional limits
options.B: Indian secularism requires complete separation of religion and State
options.C: Indian secularism establishes a state religion
options.D: Indian secularism has no relation to the Constitution

questions.explanation: Indian secularism is not always described as an absolute wall of separation. The State must maintain constitutional neutrality and equal respect while it may engage with religious institutions for reform, regulation of secular activities or protection of rights, subject to constitutional limits.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is religious neutrality of the State?

options.A: The State does not establish or favour an official religion and must treat citizens equally regardless of religious belief
options.B: The State promotes one particular religion
options.D: The State has no role in religious matters

questions.explanation: Religious neutrality means that the State does not establish or favour an official religion and must treat citizens equally regardless of religious belief, subject to constitutional provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is communalism and how is it different from secularisation?

options.A: Communalism politicises religious identity in ways that may create hostility between communities; secularisation concerns changes in the social authority and institutional role of religion
options.B: Communalism and secularisation are the same

questions.explanation: Communalism politicises religious identity in ways that may create hostility or division between communities. Secularisation concerns changes in the social authority and institutional role of religion; the concepts describe different phenomena.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of secularisation in modern society?

options.A: It can support specialised public institutions, evidence-based policy and equal civic participation across religious communities
options.D: It has no role in modern society

questions.explanation: Secularisation can support specialised public institutions, evidence-based policy and equal civic participation across religious communities. Its effects differ according to social history and political institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a common debate about secularisation in India?

options.A: The public role of religion

questions.explanation: Debates concern the public role of religion, minority rights, personal laws, State regulation of religious institutions, religious conversion, communal politics and the meaning of equal treatment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is globalisation?

options.A: The growing interconnectedness and interdependence of countries, societies and economies through trade, investment, technology, migration, communication, culture and the movement of information and ideas
options.B: The isolation of countries from each other

questions.explanation: Globalisation is the growing interconnectedness and interdependence of countries, societies and economies through trade, investment, technology, migration, communication, culture and the movement of information and ideas.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major dimensions of globalisation?

options.A: Economic, political, technological, cultural, social and environmental

questions.explanation: The major dimensions are economic, political, technological, cultural, social and environmental globalisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is economic globalisation?

options.A: The increasing integration of national economies through international trade, foreign investment, global production networks, financial flows and movement of services and technology
options.B: The spread of cultural products across borders
options.C: The influence of international organisations on national policy

questions.explanation: Economic globalisation is the increasing integration of national economies through international trade, foreign investment, global production networks, financial flows and movement of services and technology.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is cultural globalisation?

options.A: The spread and exchange of cultural products, ideas, languages, lifestyles, entertainment, food practices and values across national borders

questions.explanation: Cultural globalisation is the spread and exchange of cultural products, ideas, languages, lifestyles, entertainment, food practices and values across national borders.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is political globalisation?

options.A: The growing influence of international organisations, treaties, transnational movements and cross-border issues on national policy and governance

questions.explanation: Political globalisation refers to the growing influence of international organisations, treaties, transnational movements and cross-border issues on national policy and governance.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is technological globalisation?

options.A: The worldwide spread and interconnection of technologies, digital networks, scientific knowledge and communication systems

questions.explanation: Technological globalisation refers to the worldwide spread and interconnection of technologies, digital networks, scientific knowledge and communication systems.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a major factor driving globalisation?

options.A: Developments in information and communication technology

questions.explanation: Developments in information and communication technology, transport, international trade, multinational companies, financial integration, migration, international agreements and policy changes have accelerated globalisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a multinational corporation?

options.A: A company that owns, controls or coordinates business activities in more than one country
options.B: A company that operates in only one country

questions.explanation: A multinational corporation is a company that owns, controls or coordinates business activities in more than one country.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is foreign direct investment (FDI)?

options.A: Investment by an individual or enterprise from one country into a business or productive asset in another country, generally involving a lasting interest or significant influence
options.D: Investment only in the stock market

questions.explanation: Foreign direct investment (FDI) is investment by an individual or enterprise from one country into a business or productive asset in another country, generally involving a lasting interest or significant influence in the enterprise.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is liberalisation?

options.A: The reduction or removal of certain government restrictions and controls on economic activity, trade, investment or industry
options.B: The increase of government restrictions on the economy
options.C: The transfer of ownership from private to public sector
options.D: The sale of government equity in public sector enterprises

questions.explanation: Liberalisation is the reduction or removal of certain government restrictions and controls on economic activity, trade, investment or industry, subject to the policy framework adopted by a country.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is privatisation?

options.A: The transfer of ownership, management or control of an enterprise or activity from the public sector to private entities
options.B: The increase of government control over the economy
options.C: The reduction of government restrictions on the economy
options.D: The sale of government equity in public sector enterprises

questions.explanation: Privatisation is the transfer of ownership, management or control of an enterprise or activity from the public sector to private entities, in whole or in part.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is disinvestment?

options.A: The sale by the government of part or all of its equity in a public sector enterprise
options.B: The transfer of ownership from private to public sector
options.C: The reduction of government restrictions on the economy
options.D: Investment by foreign companies in domestic businesses

questions.explanation: Disinvestment is the sale by the government of part or all of its equity in a public sector enterprise. It may or may not result in transfer of management control.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the meaning of LPG reforms in India?

options.A: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation

questions.explanation: LPG refers to Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation. The major economic reforms initiated in 1991 included industrial delicensing in many sectors, trade and investment policy changes, financial-sector reforms and measures to increase competition and integration with the world economy.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Who was the Prime Minister of India when the major 1991 economic reforms were initiated?

options.A: P. V. Narasimha Rao

questions.explanation: P. V. Narasimha Rao was Prime Minister when the major economic reforms of 1991 were initiated. Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister and played a central role in formulating and presenting the reform programme.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What was the role of Dr. Manmohan Singh in the 1991 economic reforms?

options.A: As Finance Minister, he presented the Union Budget associated with the reform programme and was a key architect of India's economic liberalisation measures
options.B: He was the Prime Minister during the reforms
options.C: He was the President of India
options.D: He had no role in the reforms

questions.explanation: As Finance Minister in 1991, Dr. Manmohan Singh presented the Union Budget associated with the reform programme and was a key architect of India's economic liberalisation measures.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a positive effect of globalisation?

options.A: Expanded markets

questions.explanation: Potential benefits include expanded markets, foreign investment, technology transfer, access to global knowledge, export opportunities, consumer choice, international collaboration and growth in some service and manufacturing sectors.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a negative effect of globalisation?

options.A: Unequal gains

questions.explanation: Challenges can include unequal gains, pressure on small producers, job insecurity in some sectors, dependence on global markets, cultural homogenisation, environmental costs, financial volatility and vulnerability to international crises.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is cultural homogenisation?

options.A: The tendency for cultural practices, products or lifestyles to become more similar across societies, sometimes at the expense of local distinctiveness
options.B: The blending of elements from different cultures
options.C: The gap in access to digital technologies
options.D: The spread of Western culture only

questions.explanation: Cultural homogenisation is the tendency for cultural practices, products or lifestyles to become more similar across societies, sometimes at the expense of local distinctiveness.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is cultural hybridisation?

options.A: The creation of new cultural forms through the blending and adaptation of elements from different cultures
options.B: The tendency for cultures to become more similar
options.C: The gap in access to digital technologies
options.D: The rejection of all foreign culture

questions.explanation: Cultural hybridisation is the creation of new cultural forms through the blending and adaptation of elements from different cultures.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the digital divide?

options.A: The gap between individuals or communities in access to digital devices, internet connectivity, digital skills and the ability to use digital services effectively
options.B: The gap between rich and poor countries
options.C: The difference between urban and rural areas
options.D: The gap between literate and illiterate people

questions.explanation: The digital divide is the gap between individuals or communities in access to digital devices, internet connectivity, digital skills and the ability to use digital services effectively.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: When was the World Trade Organization (WTO) established?

options.A: 1 January 1995

questions.explanation: The World Trade Organization (WTO), established on 1 January 1995, provides a framework for international trade rules, negotiations and dispute settlement among its members.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?

options.A: It provides a framework for international trade rules, negotiations and dispute settlement among its members
options.B: It provides financial assistance to member countries
options.D: It provides financing for development and poverty reduction

questions.explanation: The World Trade Organization (WTO), established on 1 January 1995, provides a framework for international trade rules, negotiations and dispute settlement among its members.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?

options.A: It promotes international monetary cooperation and financial stability, supports global trade and growth, and provides policy advice and financial assistance to member countries
options.B: It provides a framework for international trade rules
options.C: It provides financing for development and poverty reduction

questions.explanation: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) promotes international monetary cooperation and financial stability, supports global trade and growth, and provides policy advice and financial assistance to member countries subject to its mandate.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of the World Bank?

options.A: It provides financing, knowledge and technical assistance for development and poverty reduction
options.B: It provides a framework for international trade rules

questions.explanation: The World Bank Group provides financing, knowledge and technical assistance for development and poverty reduction. The term 'World Bank' commonly refers to the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of information technology in globalisation?

options.A: It enables rapid communication, digital trade, remote work, global supply-chain coordination, online education, financial services and cross-border exchange of information
options.B: It has no role in globalisation

questions.explanation: Information technology enables rapid communication, digital trade, remote work, global supply-chain coordination, online education, financial services and cross-border exchange of information.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How has globalisation affected Indian society?

options.A: It has influenced employment, consumption, media, education, migration, food, fashion, technology, business and aspirations
options.B: It has had no impact on Indian society
options.C: It has only benefited rural areas
options.D: It has only affected urban areas

questions.explanation: Globalisation has influenced employment, consumption, media, education, migration, food, fashion, technology, business and aspirations. Its benefits and costs are distributed unevenly across regions, occupations and social groups.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between globalisation and liberalisation?

options.A: Globalisation is the growing worldwide interconnectedness of economies and societies, while liberalisation is a policy process that reduces selected restrictions

questions.explanation: Globalisation is the growing worldwide interconnectedness of economies and societies. Liberalisation is a policy process that reduces selected restrictions or controls and may facilitate greater integration.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between globalisation and Westernisation?

options.A: Globalisation involves multidirectional cross-border flows among many countries and cultures, while Westernisation specifically refers to influence from Western societies
options.D: Globalisation refers only to Western influence

questions.explanation: Globalisation involves multidirectional cross-border flows among many countries and cultures. Westernisation specifically refers to influence from Western societies and institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is industrialisation?

options.A: The process through which an economy develops and expands manufacturing and other industrial activities, often accompanied by mechanisation and technological change

questions.explanation: Industrialisation is the process through which an economy develops and expands manufacturing and other industrial activities, often accompanied by mechanisation, technological change, factory production, capital investment and occupational transformation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a major characteristic of industrialisation?

options.A: Factory-based production

questions.explanation: Major characteristics include factory-based production, use of machinery, division of labour, specialisation, large-scale production, wage employment, capital investment, technological innovation and growth of industrial infrastructure.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following promotes industrialisation?

options.A: Capital

questions.explanation: Capital, raw materials, energy, labour, technology, transport, markets, infrastructure, entrepreneurship, government policy, financial institutions and stable institutions can promote industrialisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Industrial Revolution?

options.A: The major transformation in production that began in Britain in the eighteenth century involving mechanisation, factory systems, new energy sources and changes in transport and labour

questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution refers to the major transformation in production that began in Britain in the eighteenth century and spread to other regions, involving mechanisation, factory systems, new energy sources and changes in transport and labour.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between industrialisation and industrial growth?

options.A: Industrial growth refers to an increase in industrial output or activity, while industrialisation is a broader structural transformation in which industry becomes a more important part of production, employment, technology and social organisation
options.C: Industrialisation refers only to output increase
options.D: Industrial growth is broader than industrialisation

questions.explanation: Industrial growth refers to an increase in industrial output or activity. Industrialisation is a broader structural transformation in which industry becomes a more important part of production, employment, technology and social organisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is division of labour in industry?

options.A: The separation of a production process into specialised tasks performed by different workers or units
options.B: The equal distribution of work among all workers
options.C: The reduction of labour in production
options.D: The replacement of workers by machines

questions.explanation: Division of labour is the separation of a production process into specialised tasks performed by different workers or units, often increasing efficiency and output.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is mechanisation?

options.A: The use of machines to perform tasks previously carried out wholly or partly by human or animal labour
options.B: The reduction of machines in production
options.C: The use of control systems to reduce human intervention
options.D: The centralisation of workers in factories

questions.explanation: Mechanisation is the use of machines to perform tasks previously carried out wholly or partly by human or animal labour.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is automation?

options.A: The use of control systems, machinery and software to perform processes with reduced direct human intervention
options.B: The use of machines to replace all human labour
options.C: The separation of production into specialised tasks
options.D: The centralisation of workers in factories

questions.explanation: Automation is the use of control systems, machinery and software to perform processes with reduced direct human intervention.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the factory system?

options.A: A mode of production in which workers, machines and materials are brought together in a central workplace under organised management
options.B: A system of production in homes
options.D: A system of trade and commerce

questions.explanation: The factory system is a mode of production in which workers, machines and materials are brought together in a central workplace under organised management to produce goods, usually on a large scale.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between industrialisation and urbanisation?

options.A: Industrialisation often attracts workers to industrial centres and promotes the growth of towns and cities, but the two are related yet not identical

questions.explanation: Industrialisation often attracts workers to industrial centres and promotes the growth of towns and cities. Urbanisation can also occur through service-sector growth, administration, education and other processes, so the two are related but not identical.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a positive effect of industrialisation?

options.A: Increased production

questions.explanation: Potential benefits include increased production, employment, technological development, infrastructure, export capacity, occupational specialisation and growth in income and productivity.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a negative effect of industrialisation?

options.A: Pollution

questions.explanation: Challenges may include pollution, occupational hazards, unsafe working conditions, displacement, informal labour, regional inequality, resource depletion, congestion and unequal distribution of industrial gains.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is deindustrialisation?

options.A: A decline in the relative importance of manufacturing or industrial employment in an economy or region

questions.explanation: Deindustrialisation is a decline in the relative importance of manufacturing or industrial employment in an economy or region. It can result from structural change, automation, global competition, policy changes or industrial decline.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the organised sector?

options.A: Enterprises and employment operating within formal legal and regulatory frameworks, with required records and applicable labour protections
options.B: Economic activities with limited formal registration

questions.explanation: The organised sector generally consists of enterprises and employment operating within formal legal and regulatory frameworks, with required records and applicable labour protections.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the unorganised or informal sector?

options.A: Economic activities and workers with varying degrees of limited formal registration, job security, written contracts and social protection
options.B: Enterprises operating within formal legal frameworks

questions.explanation: The unorganised or informal sector includes economic activities and workers with varying degrees of limited formal registration, job security, written contracts and social protection. Legal definitions depend on the context and law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between industrialisation and the working class?

options.A: Industrialisation expands wage labour and can create an industrial working class dependent on wages
options.C: Industrialisation has no effect on the working class

questions.explanation: Industrialisation expands wage labour and can create an industrial working class whose members depend on wages and work in factories, mines, construction, transport and related sectors.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a trade union?

options.A: An organisation of workers formed to protect and advance their employment-related interests

questions.explanation: A trade union is an organisation of workers formed to protect and advance their employment-related interests, including wages, working conditions, rights and collective bargaining.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is collective bargaining?

options.A: The process through which employers and workers' representatives negotiate terms and conditions of employment
options.B: The process of individual wage negotiation
options.C: The process of government regulation of wages

questions.explanation: Collective bargaining is the process through which employers and workers' representatives negotiate terms and conditions of employment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the importance of labour welfare?

options.A: It seeks to protect workers' health, safety, dignity and well-being through fair conditions, social security, workplace facilities and legal safeguards
options.B: It seeks to reduce workers' wages
options.C: It seeks to increase working hours
options.D: It seeks to eliminate trade unions

questions.explanation: Labour welfare measures seek to protect workers' health, safety, dignity and well-being through fair conditions, social security, workplace facilities and legal safeguards.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of industrial policy?

options.A: Government measures that influence industrial development through infrastructure, incentives, regulation, investment, technology, skills, trade and support for particular sectors

questions.explanation: Industrial policy refers to government measures that influence industrial development through infrastructure, incentives, regulation, investment, technology, skills, trade and support for particular sectors.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: When was the Make in India initiative launched?

options.A: September 2014

questions.explanation: Make in India was launched by the Government of India in September 2014 to encourage manufacturing, investment, innovation, skill development and improvement in the business environment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme?

options.A: Schemes that provide incentives linked to incremental production or sales in selected sectors
options.B: Schemes that provide subsidies for agriculture

questions.explanation: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes provide incentives linked to incremental production or sales in selected sectors, subject to sector-specific guidelines and eligibility conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is sustainable industrialisation?

options.A: Expanding productive industrial activity while improving resource efficiency, worker safety and environmental performance and reducing pollution and emissions
options.B: Expanding industrial activity without any environmental concerns

questions.explanation: Sustainable industrialisation seeks to expand productive industrial activity while improving resource efficiency, worker safety and environmental performance and reducing pollution and emissions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is urbanisation?

options.A: The process by which an increasing proportion of a population lives in urban areas, accompanied by the growth, expansion or reclassification of towns and cities
options.C: The process of rural development only

questions.explanation: Urbanisation is the process by which an increasing proportion of a population lives in urban areas, accompanied by the growth, expansion or reclassification of towns and cities and changes in economic and social life.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a major cause of urbanisation?

options.A: Rural-to-urban migration
options.B: Natural population growth in urban settlements

questions.explanation: Rural-to-urban migration, natural population growth in urban settlements, industrialisation, expansion of services, education, employment opportunities, infrastructure development and reclassification of settlements contribute to urbanisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is rural-to-urban migration?

options.A: The movement of people from villages or countryside areas to towns and cities, temporarily or permanently
options.B: The movement of people from cities to villages
options.C: The movement of people between two cities
options.D: The movement of people between two villages

questions.explanation: Rural-to-urban migration is the movement of people from villages or countryside areas to towns and cities, temporarily or permanently, often for work, education, healthcare or other opportunities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are push factors of migration?

options.A: Conditions that encourage people to leave a place, such as unemployment, low income, landlessness, drought, conflict, poor services or lack of educational opportunities
options.B: Conditions that attract people to a destination

questions.explanation: Push factors are conditions that encourage people to leave a place, such as unemployment, low income, landlessness, drought, conflict, poor services or lack of educational opportunities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are pull factors of migration?

options.A: Conditions that attract people to a destination, such as jobs, higher wages, education, healthcare, transport, safety and better access to services
options.B: Conditions that encourage people to leave a place

questions.explanation: Pull factors are conditions that attract people to a destination, such as jobs, higher wages, education, healthcare, transport, safety and better access to services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is an urban agglomeration in Indian Census terminology?

options.A: A continuous urban spread consisting of a town and its adjoining outgrowths, or two or more physically contiguous towns with or without outgrowths
options.B: A single city with no surrounding areas

questions.explanation: An urban agglomeration is a continuous urban spread consisting of a town and its adjoining outgrowths, or two or more physically contiguous towns with or without outgrowths, as defined by the Census of India.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a census town?

options.A: A settlement that meets the Census of India's specified demographic and occupational criteria for an urban area but is not necessarily governed as a statutory municipality
options.B: A town with a municipal corporation

questions.explanation: A census town is a settlement that meets the Census of India's specified demographic and occupational criteria for an urban area but is not necessarily governed as a statutory municipality. The commonly applied criteria include a minimum population of 5,000, population density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre, and at least 75 per cent of male main workers engaged in non-agricultural pursuits.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the minimum population required for a settlement to be classified as a census town in India?
questions.explanation: The commonly applied criteria for a census town include a minimum population of 5,000.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the minimum population density required for a settlement to be classified as a census town in India?

options.A: 400 persons per square kilometre

questions.explanation: The commonly applied criteria for a census town include a population density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What percentage of male main workers must be engaged in non-agricultural pursuits for a settlement to be classified as a census town?

options.A: At least 75 per cent

questions.explanation: The commonly applied criteria for a census town include at least 75 per cent of male main workers engaged in non-agricultural pursuits.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a statutory town?

options.A: A place with an urban local body such as a municipality, municipal corporation, cantonment board or notified town area committee
options.B: A settlement that meets census criteria but has no local body

questions.explanation: A statutory town is a place with an urban local body such as a municipality, municipal corporation, cantonment board or notified town area committee, as recognised under applicable law and Census classification.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How does Article 243P(c) define a metropolitan area?

options.A: An area with a population of ten lakh or more, comprising one or more districts and two or more municipalities or Panchayats or other contiguous areas
options.B: An area with a population of one lakh or more
options.C: An area with a population of five lakh or more
options.D: An area with a population of fifty lakh or more

questions.explanation: Article 243P(c) defines a metropolitan area as an area with a population of ten lakh or more, comprising one or more districts and two or more municipalities or Panchayats or other contiguous areas, specified by the Governor by public notification for the purposes of Part IXA.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is urban sprawl?

options.A: The outward, often low-density and poorly coordinated expansion of urban development into surrounding rural or peri-urban areas

questions.explanation: Urban sprawl is the outward, often low-density and poorly coordinated expansion of urban development into surrounding rural or peri-urban areas.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a slum?

options.A: A densely populated urban settlement or area characterised by inadequate housing and deficiencies in basic services

questions.explanation: A slum is a densely populated urban settlement or area characterised by inadequate housing and deficiencies in basic services such as safe water, sanitation, drainage, roads or secure tenure. Definitions vary across laws and surveys.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a major problem associated with rapid urbanisation?

options.A: Housing shortages

questions.explanation: Problems may include housing shortages, informal settlements, traffic congestion, air and water pollution, inadequate drainage, waste-management difficulties, pressure on water and energy, unemployment or informal work, inequality and overstretched civic services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is urban poverty?

options.A: Deprivation among people living in towns and cities, including inadequate income, insecure work, poor housing, limited access to essential services and vulnerability to high living costs

questions.explanation: Urban poverty is deprivation among people living in towns and cities, including inadequate income, insecure work, poor housing, limited access to essential services and vulnerability to high living costs.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between urbanisation and urban growth?

options.A: Urban growth is an increase in the population or physical size of an urban settlement, while urbanisation is a broader process involving a rising share of the population living in urban areas
options.C: Urbanisation refers only to population increase
options.D: Urban growth is broader than urbanisation

questions.explanation: Urban growth is an increase in the population or physical size of an urban settlement. Urbanisation is a broader process involving a rising share of the population living in urban areas and changes in social and economic structure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to urban local bodies?

options.A: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992

questions.explanation: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, inserted Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule concerning municipalities. Its principal provisions came into force on 1 June 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When did the principal provisions of the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act come into force?

options.A: 1 June 1993

questions.explanation: The principal provisions of the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, came into force on 1 June 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are the three types of municipalities provided under Article 243Q?

options.A: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation
options.B: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad
options.C: Town Committee, City Council and Metropolitan Authority
options.D: Village Council, Block Council and District Council

questions.explanation: Article 243Q provides for a Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area, a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area and a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area, subject to constitutional criteria and State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: For what type of area is a Nagar Panchayat constituted under Article 243Q?

options.A: A transitional area

questions.explanation: Article 243Q provides for a Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: For what type of area is a Municipal Council constituted under Article 243Q?

options.A: A smaller urban area

questions.explanation: Article 243Q provides for a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: For what type of area is a Municipal Corporation constituted under Article 243Q?

options.A: A larger urban area

questions.explanation: Article 243Q provides for a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How many functions are listed in the Twelfth Schedule that may be entrusted to municipalities?
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions that may be entrusted to municipalities under Article 243W, including urban planning, regulation of land use, roads, water supply, public health, sanitation, solid-waste management and urban poverty alleviation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article may the Twelfth Schedule functions be entrusted to municipalities?

options.A: Article 243W

questions.explanation: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions that may be entrusted to municipalities under Article 243W.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is included in the Twelfth Schedule functions of municipalities?

options.A: Urban planning and regulation of land use
options.C: Public health, sanitation and solid-waste management

questions.explanation: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions including urban planning, regulation of land use, roads, water supply, public health, sanitation, solid-waste management and urban poverty alleviation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: When was the Smart Cities Mission launched by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The Smart Cities Mission was launched by the Government of India in 2015 to promote sustainable and inclusive urban development through area-based development and pan-city solutions, including technology-enabled improvements.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the objective of the Smart Cities Mission?

options.A: To promote sustainable and inclusive urban development through area-based development and pan-city solutions

questions.explanation: The Smart Cities Mission was launched in 2015 to promote sustainable and inclusive urban development through area-based development and pan-city solutions, including technology-enabled improvements.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does AMRUT stand for?

options.A: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
options.B: Atal Mission for Rural and Urban Transformation
options.C: Atal Mission for Regional and Urban Transport
options.D: Atal Mission for Renewable and Urban Technology

questions.explanation: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) is a Government of India urban mission focused on basic infrastructure such as water supply, sewerage and septage management, storm-water drainage, green spaces and non-motorised urban transport.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does AMRUT focus on?

options.A: Basic infrastructure such as water supply, sewerage, storm-water drainage, green spaces and non-motorised urban transport

questions.explanation: AMRUT is a Government of India urban mission focused on basic infrastructure such as water supply, sewerage and septage management, storm-water drainage, green spaces and non-motorised urban transport.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is sustainable urbanisation?

options.A: Urban development that is inclusive, economically viable and environmentally responsible, with adequate housing, public transport, water, sanitation, green spaces, resilient infrastructure and effective local governance
options.B: Urban development without any environmental concerns

questions.explanation: Sustainable urbanisation is urban development that is inclusive, economically viable and environmentally responsible, with adequate housing, public transport, water, sanitation, green spaces, resilient infrastructure and effective local governance.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between urbanisation and social change?

options.A: Urbanisation changes family patterns, occupations, social networks, lifestyles, gender roles, consumption, political participation and access to education and services
options.B: Urbanisation has no effect on society

questions.explanation: Urbanisation changes family patterns, occupations, social networks, lifestyles, gender roles, consumption, political participation and access to education and services. It can create opportunities as well as new inequalities and pressures.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is social mobility?

options.A: The movement of individuals or groups from one social position or status to another within a system of social stratification
options.B: The movement of people from one place to another
options.C: The movement of goods and services
options.D: The movement of capital across borders

questions.explanation: Social mobility is the movement of individuals or groups from one social position or status to another within a system of social stratification.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Who made an influential contribution to the systematic study of social mobility, especially in the work 'Social Mobility' published in 1927?

options.A: Pitirim A. Sorokin

questions.explanation: Pitirim A. Sorokin made an influential contribution to the systematic study of social mobility, especially in his work Social Mobility, published in 1927.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: In which year was Pitirim A. Sorokin's work 'Social Mobility' published?
questions.explanation: Pitirim A. Sorokin's work Social Mobility was published in 1927.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the two broad forms of social mobility based on direction?

options.A: Horizontal mobility and vertical mobility

questions.explanation: The two broad forms of social mobility based on direction are horizontal mobility and vertical mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is horizontal social mobility?

options.A: Movement from one social position to another at broadly the same level of social status
options.B: Movement upward in the social hierarchy
options.C: Movement downward in the social hierarchy

questions.explanation: Horizontal mobility is movement from one social position to another at broadly the same level of social status, such as a teacher moving to a similar teaching post in another institution.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is vertical social mobility?

options.A: Movement upward or downward in the social hierarchy, involving a change in social status, class position, income, power or prestige
options.B: Movement at the same level of social status

questions.explanation: Vertical mobility is movement upward or downward in the social hierarchy, involving a change in social status, class position, income, power or prestige.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is upward social mobility?

options.A: Movement to a higher social position
options.B: Movement to a lower social position

questions.explanation: Upward mobility is movement to a higher social position, for example when a person from a low-income background obtains a professional qualification and enters a substantially higher-paid occupation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is downward social mobility?

options.A: Movement to a lower social position
options.B: Movement to a higher social position

questions.explanation: Downward mobility is movement to a lower social position, for example when a person loses a stable high-income occupation and experiences a major decline in income and status.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is intergenerational mobility?

options.A: A change in social or economic position between one generation and the next
options.B: A change in position during an individual's own lifetime
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement due to structural changes in the economy

questions.explanation: Intergenerational mobility is a change in social or economic position between one generation and the next, such as a child's occupational position differing from that of their parents.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is intragenerational mobility?

options.A: A change in an individual's social or economic position during that person's own lifetime
options.B: A change in position between one generation and the next
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement due to structural changes in the economy

questions.explanation: Intragenerational mobility is a change in an individual's social or economic position during that person's own lifetime.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is structural mobility?

options.A: Mobility that occurs when broad changes in the economy or social structure alter the number or distribution of positions
options.B: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement during an individual's lifetime only

questions.explanation: Structural mobility occurs when broad changes in the economy or social structure alter the number or distribution of positions, enabling or requiring many people to move between occupational or class categories.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is exchange mobility?

options.A: Movement in which individuals or groups exchange positions within a relatively stable hierarchy, so that upward movement by some is accompanied by downward movement by others
options.B: Movement due to structural changes in the economy
options.D: Movement at the same level of social status

questions.explanation: Exchange mobility refers to movement in which individuals or groups exchange positions within a relatively stable hierarchy, so that upward movement by some is accompanied by downward movement by others. It is a theoretical category.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is occupational mobility?

options.A: Movement from one occupation to another, which may involve a change in skill, income, prestige, working conditions or social status
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement due to structural changes in the economy

questions.explanation: Occupational mobility is movement from one occupation to another, which may involve a change in skill, income, prestige, working conditions or social status.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is educational mobility?

options.A: Movement between levels or forms of educational attainment, often across generations or during an individual's life
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement due to structural changes in the economy

questions.explanation: Educational mobility refers to movement between levels or forms of educational attainment, often across generations or during an individual's life. It can influence occupational and class mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is caste mobility?

options.A: Changes in the social position, recognition or influence of caste groups over time
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status

questions.explanation: Caste mobility refers to changes in the social position, recognition or influence of caste groups over time. It may occur through economic change, political mobilisation, education, social reform and changes in local power relations, but caste identity is not simply interchangeable with class position.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following promotes social mobility?

options.A: Education and professional skills

questions.explanation: Education, professional skills, economic growth, industrialisation, urbanisation, migration, access to capital and land, fair recruitment, anti-discrimination measures and public welfare policies can promote mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a barrier to social mobility?

options.A: Poverty

questions.explanation: Poverty, unequal education, caste discrimination, gender inequality, disability-related barriers, inherited wealth disparities, regional inequality, lack of networks and insecure employment can restrict mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between education and social mobility?

options.A: Education can provide qualifications, skills and access to occupations that improve income and status, but its effect depends on educational quality, affordability, labour-market opportunities and removal of discrimination
options.C: Education has no relation to social mobility

questions.explanation: Education can provide qualifications, skills and access to occupations that improve income and status. Its effect depends on educational quality, affordability, labour-market opportunities and the removal of discrimination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between urbanisation and social mobility?

options.A: Urbanisation can create access to diverse occupations, education, markets and social networks, supporting mobility, but high living costs and unequal access can limit opportunities
options.C: Urbanisation has no relation to social mobility

questions.explanation: Urbanisation can create access to diverse occupations, education, markets and social networks, supporting mobility. However, high living costs, informal employment and unequal access to housing and services can limit these opportunities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between industrialisation and social mobility?

options.A: Industrialisation can create new occupations, wage employment, technical skills and professional opportunities, allowing some people to move beyond inherited occupations
options.C: Industrialisation has no relation to social mobility

questions.explanation: Industrialisation can create new occupations, wage employment, technical skills and professional opportunities, allowing some people to move beyond inherited occupations. The extent of mobility depends on labour conditions, education and access to jobs.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is achieved status?

options.A: Status acquired through a person's actions, qualifications or accomplishments
options.D: Status based on inherited social position

questions.explanation: Achieved status is acquired through a person's actions, qualifications or accomplishments.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is ascribed status?

options.A: Status assigned at birth or independently of individual choice, such as age or inherited social position

questions.explanation: Ascribed status is assigned at birth or independently of individual choice, such as age or inherited social position in many social systems.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is meritocracy?

options.A: An ideal system in which positions and rewards are allocated according to ability, achievement and performance
options.B: A system based on inherited status

questions.explanation: Meritocracy is an ideal system in which positions and rewards are allocated according to ability, achievement and performance. In practice, unequal starting conditions can affect how fairly merit is assessed.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is social stratification and how is it related to social mobility?

options.A: Social stratification is the structured ranking of groups in society; social mobility describes movement between positions within that hierarchy
options.C: Social mobility is the ranking of groups
