options.D: Social stratification describes movement between positions

questions.explanation: Social stratification is the structured ranking of groups in society. Social mobility describes movement between positions within that hierarchy or changes to the hierarchy itself.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can social mobility eliminate social inequality completely?

options.A: No, mobility can change the position of individuals or groups but does not automatically remove unequal access to wealth, power, education, social networks or opportunities
options.C: Yes, mobility eliminates all forms of inequality
options.D: No, mobility has no effect on inequality

questions.explanation: No. Mobility can change the position of individuals or groups, but it does not automatically remove unequal access to wealth, power, education, social networks or opportunities. Structural reforms may also be needed.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is absolute mobility?

options.A: A measure of whether people have moved to different positions compared with their parents or earlier generations
options.B: A measure of the strength of the relationship between origins and destinations
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement due to structural changes only

questions.explanation: Absolute mobility measures whether people have moved to different positions compared with their parents or earlier generations, often due to changes in the occupational structure.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is relative mobility?

options.A: A measure of the strength of the relationship between people's origins and destinations, or their chances of reaching positions compared with others
options.B: A measure of whether people have moved to different positions compared with their parents
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement due to structural changes only

questions.explanation: Relative mobility measures the strength of the relationship between people's origins and destinations, or their chances of reaching positions compared with others.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the significance of social mobility in a democratic society?

options.A: It can widen opportunities, reduce inherited disadvantage, support social justice and allow people to participate more fully in economic and public life
options.B: It has no significance in a democracy
options.D: It prevents participation in public life

questions.explanation: Social mobility can widen opportunities, reduce inherited disadvantage, support social justice and allow people to participate more fully in economic and public life. Equal opportunity and protection against discrimination are important conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the main difference between modernisation and Westernisation?

options.A: Modernisation is broad structural transformation involving technology, economy, education and institutions; Westernisation is influence from or adoption of practices and institutions associated with Western societies
options.D: Modernisation refers only to Western influence

questions.explanation: Modernisation is broad structural transformation involving technology, economy, education and institutions; Westernisation is influence from or adoption of practices and institutions associated with Western societies.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the main difference between secularisation and secularism?

options.A: Secularisation is a social process involving changes in the role and authority of religion; secularism is a political or constitutional principle governing the relationship between State and religion

questions.explanation: Secularisation is a social process involving changes in the role and authority of religion; secularism is a political or constitutional principle governing the relationship between State and religion.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the main difference between industrialisation and urbanisation?

options.A: Industrialisation is the expansion and transformation of industrial production; urbanisation is the growth of the urban population and settlements
options.D: Industrialisation refers only to urban growth

questions.explanation: Industrialisation is the expansion and transformation of industrial production; urbanisation is the growth of the urban population and settlements. Industrialisation can drive urbanisation, but urbanisation also occurs through services and other processes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the main difference between globalisation and modernisation?

options.A: Globalisation refers to growing cross-border interconnectedness; modernisation refers to structural transformation within societies
options.D: Globalisation refers only to Western influence

questions.explanation: Globalisation refers to growing cross-border interconnectedness; modernisation refers to structural transformation within societies. Globalisation can influence modernisation, but the terms are not interchangeable.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Indian sociologist is associated with Westernisation in Indian sociology?

options.A: M. N. Srinivas

questions.explanation: M. N. Srinivas is associated with the concept of Westernisation in Indian sociology.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Indian sociologist is associated with the modernisation of Indian tradition?

options.A: Yogendra Singh

questions.explanation: Yogendra Singh is associated with the modernisation of Indian tradition.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which scholar wrote 'Social Mobility' in 1927?

options.A: Pitirim A. Sorokin

questions.explanation: Pitirim A. Sorokin wrote Social Mobility in 1927.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: In which year were India's major LPG economic reforms initiated?
questions.explanation: India's major LPG economic reforms were initiated in 1991.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Who was India's Prime Minister when the 1991 economic reforms were initiated?

options.A: P. V. Narasimha Rao

questions.explanation: P. V. Narasimha Rao was India's Prime Minister when the 1991 economic reforms were initiated.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Who was the Finance Minister associated with presenting the 1991 reform Budget?

options.A: Dr. Manmohan Singh

questions.explanation: Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister associated with presenting the 1991 reform Budget.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: On which date did the World Trade Organization come into existence?

options.A: 1 January 1995

questions.explanation: The World Trade Organization came into existence on 1 January 1995.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted the word 'secular' into the Preamble?

options.A: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976

questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, inserted the word 'secular' into the Preamble.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to municipalities?

options.A: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992

questions.explanation: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, gave constitutional status to municipalities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted the Eleventh Schedule relating to Panchayats?

options.A: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992

questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, inserted the Eleventh Schedule relating to Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the two principal directions of vertical social mobility?

options.A: Upward mobility and downward mobility

questions.explanation: The two principal directions of vertical social mobility are upward mobility and downward mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the two main forms of mobility based on the time or generation comparison?

options.A: Intergenerational mobility and intragenerational mobility

questions.explanation: The two main forms of mobility based on time or generation comparison are intergenerational mobility and intragenerational mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the central idea of social change?

options.A: Social change is a continuing transformation in social relationships, institutions, values, norms and structures that can be gradual or rapid, planned or unplanned
options.B: Social change only refers to economic change
options.C: Social change only refers to political change
options.D: Social change only refers to cultural change

questions.explanation: Social change is a continuing transformation in social relationships, institutions, values, norms and structures. It can be gradual or rapid, planned or unplanned, and may create both opportunities and inequalities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of modernisation?

options.A: Scientific temper

questions.explanation: Modernisation does not require complete rejection of all traditions. Traditional institutions can change, adapt and sometimes gain new forms or functions under modern conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a concern associated with science and technology in modernisation?

options.A: Unequal digital access

questions.explanation: Science and technology can increase productivity and access to information, while also creating concerns such as unequal digital access, job displacement and privacy risks.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does secular-rational thinking necessarily require individuals to abandon religious belief?

options.A: Yes, it requires complete abandonment of religion
options.B: No, it does not necessarily require individuals to abandon religious belief
options.C: Yes, it prohibits all religious practices

questions.explanation: Secular-rational thinking explains social and natural events through reason, evidence and publicly testable explanations rather than relying exclusively on supernatural explanations. It does not necessarily require individuals to abandon religious belief.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is associated with modernity?

options.A: Scientific organisation

questions.explanation: Modernity is associated with newer social, economic, political and cultural arrangements such as scientific organisation, industrial economies and modern institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can traditions persist or adapt within modern societies?

options.A: No, traditions completely disappear in modern societies
options.B: Yes, traditions may persist or adapt within modern societies
options.C: No, traditions are incompatible with modernity
options.D: Yes, but only in rural areas

questions.explanation: Traditions may persist or adapt within modern societies. Modernisation in India should not be understood simply as the disappearance of tradition.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which classical sociologist analysed changing forms of social relationships in modern society?

options.A: Ferdinand Tonnies

questions.explanation: Classical sociologists such as Emile Durkheim, Max Weber and Ferdinand Tonnies analysed major transitions associated with modern society, including division of labour, rationalisation and changing forms of social relationships.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an area influenced by Westernisation in India?

options.A: Modern education

questions.explanation: Westernisation influenced modern education, English-language use, law and administration, scientific and technological knowledge, transport, communication, clothing, food habits, architecture, political ideas and some social reform movements. It did not completely replace Indian languages.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Did British rule in India serve only social progress?

options.A: Yes, British rule was purely for social progress
options.B: No, the changes also served colonial interests and were not simply acts of social progress
options.C: Yes, British rule had no colonial motives
options.D: No, British rule had no impact on Indian society

questions.explanation: British rule introduced or expanded Western-style institutions, but these changes also served colonial interests and were not simply acts of social progress.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Was access to Western education equal for all sections of Indian society?

options.A: Yes, it was equally accessible to all
options.B: No, access was unequal and closely shaped by colonial policies and social conditions
options.C: Yes, it was accessible only to the upper castes
options.D: No, it was accessible only to women

questions.explanation: Access to Western education was unequal and closely shaped by colonial policies and social conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following practices was debated and reformed due to Western influence in India?

options.A: Sati

questions.explanation: Exposure to new ideas and institutions contributed to debates and movements concerning practices such as sati, child marriage, caste discrimination, women's education and widow remarriage.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How did Indian reformers respond to Western ideas?

options.A: They interpreted and adapted ideas in their own social and historical contexts
options.B: They accepted all Western ideas without question
options.C: They rejected all Western ideas completely
options.D: They had no response to Western ideas

questions.explanation: Indian reformers interpreted and adapted ideas in their own social and historical contexts.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is Sanskritisation?

options.A: A process in which a lower-status caste or group adopts practices and customs associated with a locally influential or higher-status group
options.B: The process of adopting Western culture

questions.explanation: Sanskritisation refers to a process in which a lower-status caste or group adopts practices and customs associated with a locally influential or higher-status group, traditionally described with reference to upper-caste practices.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Has Indian society combined Western influences with indigenous traditions?

options.A: No, Indian society completely rejected Western influences
options.B: Yes, Indian society has combined Western influences with indigenous traditions and institutions in varied ways
options.C: No, Indian society completely adopted Western culture
options.D: Yes, but only in urban areas

questions.explanation: Indian society has combined Western influences with indigenous traditions and institutions in varied ways.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a limitation of Westernisation?

options.A: Cultural imitation without critical assessment

questions.explanation: Criticisms include cultural imitation without critical assessment, consumerism, cultural domination, weakening of some local practices and the colonial context in which many Western institutions were introduced.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Through which of the following can cultural diffusion occur?

options.A: Contact

questions.explanation: Cultural diffusion is the spread of cultural traits, ideas, technologies or practices from one society or group to another through contact, migration, trade, media, education or conquest.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What was the colonial objective behind the expansion of English education in India?

options.A: To create new professional and administrative groups
options.B: To facilitate colonial administration and economic objectives

questions.explanation: English education helped create new professional and administrative groups and facilitated access to Western literature, science and political ideas. Its expansion was also linked to colonial administrative and economic objectives.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Do all dimensions of secularisation necessarily occur together or at the same pace?

options.A: Yes, they always occur together
options.B: No, these dimensions do not necessarily occur together or at the same pace
options.C: Yes, they occur at the same pace

questions.explanation: The commonly discussed dimensions of secularisation do not necessarily occur together or at the same pace.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can religion remain important in personal life and politics even when some institutions become more independent of religious authority?

options.A: No, religion completely disappears
options.B: Yes, religion may remain important in personal life, community identity, public debate and politics
options.D: Yes, but only in rural areas

questions.explanation: Religion may remain important in personal life, community identity, public debate and politics even when some institutions become more independent of religious authority.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which word was inserted into the Preamble along with 'secular' by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?

options.A: Socialist

questions.explanation: The word 'secular' was inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, along with the word 'socialist'.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following was already protected in the original Constitution before the 42nd Amendment?

options.A: Freedom of conscience and religion

questions.explanation: The original Constitution already contained important protections for freedom of conscience and religion, including Articles 25 to 28, as well as equality and minority cultural and educational rights.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion subject to which conditions?

options.A: Public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III

questions.explanation: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 26 protects the rights of religious denominations subject to which conditions?

options.A: Public order, morality and health

questions.explanation: Article 26 protects the rights of religious denominations or sections thereof to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage religious affairs, and own and administer property in accordance with law, subject to public order, morality and health.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Does Indian secularism require an absolute wall of separation between religion and State?

options.A: Yes, it requires absolute separation
options.B: No, Indian secularism is not always described as an absolute wall of separation
options.C: Yes, the State cannot engage with religious institutions
options.D: No, the State establishes an official religion

questions.explanation: Indian secularism is not always described as an absolute wall of separation. The State must maintain constitutional neutrality and equal respect while it may engage with religious institutions for reform, regulation of secular activities or protection of rights, subject to constitutional limits.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Does the State have any role in regulating secular activities associated with religion?

options.A: No, the State cannot regulate any religious activity
options.B: Yes, the State may regulate secular activities associated with religion and undertake social reform within constitutional limits
options.C: Yes, the State can regulate all religious activities without limits
options.D: No, the State has no role in religion

questions.explanation: The State may regulate secular activities associated with religion and undertake social reform within constitutional limits.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a debate about secularisation in India?

options.A: Personal laws

questions.explanation: Debates concern the public role of religion, minority rights, personal laws, State regulation of religious institutions, religious conversion, communal politics and the meaning of equal treatment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a dimension of globalisation?

options.A: Economic

questions.explanation: The major dimensions are economic, political, technological, cultural, social and environmental globalisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does FDI stand for?

options.A: Foreign Direct Investment

questions.explanation: FDI stands for Foreign Direct Investment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does LPG stand for in the context of Indian economic reforms?

options.A: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation

questions.explanation: LPG refers to Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What did the 1991 economic reforms include?

options.A: Industrial delicensing in many sectors

questions.explanation: The major economic reforms initiated in 1991 included industrial delicensing in many sectors, trade and investment policy changes, financial-sector reforms and measures to increase competition and integration with the world economy.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of globalisation?

options.A: Access to global knowledge

questions.explanation: Potential benefits include expanded markets, foreign investment, technology transfer, access to global knowledge, export opportunities, consumer choice, international collaboration and growth in some service and manufacturing sectors.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a challenge of globalisation?

options.A: Dependence on global markets

questions.explanation: Challenges can include unequal gains, pressure on small producers, job insecurity in some sectors, dependence on global markets, cultural homogenisation, environmental costs, financial volatility and vulnerability to international crises.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of cultural hybridisation?

options.A: The creation of new cultural forms through the blending of elements from different cultures
options.B: The tendency for cultures to become more similar
options.C: The rejection of all foreign culture
options.D: The spread of one culture to all societies

questions.explanation: Cultural hybridisation is the creation of new cultural forms through the blending and adaptation of elements from different cultures.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does globalisation benefit all regions, occupations and social groups equally?

options.A: Yes, it benefits all equally
options.B: No, its benefits and costs are distributed unevenly across regions, occupations and social groups
options.C: Yes, it benefits only urban areas
options.D: No, it benefits only rural areas

questions.explanation: Globalisation has influenced employment, consumption, media, education, migration, food, fashion, technology, business and aspirations. Its benefits and costs are distributed unevenly across regions, occupations and social groups.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an environmental dimension of globalisation?

options.A: Cross-border environmental issues and global environmental governance

questions.explanation: Environmental globalisation refers to cross-border environmental issues, global environmental governance and the worldwide environmental impact of economic and social integration.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a social dimension of globalisation?

options.A: Cross-border migration and social networks

questions.explanation: Social globalisation includes cross-border migration, social networks, the spread of ideas and lifestyles, and changes in social relationships across national borders.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of multinational companies in globalisation?

options.A: They coordinate business activities across countries and drive foreign investment, trade and technology transfer
options.B: They only operate within one country
options.C: They have no role in globalisation

questions.explanation: Multinational companies own, control or coordinate business activities in more than one country and are major drivers of foreign investment, trade, production networks and technology transfer.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between FDI and portfolio investment?

options.A: FDI generally involves a lasting interest or significant influence in the enterprise, while portfolio investment involves buying financial assets without such control
options.C: Portfolio investment involves control of the enterprise

questions.explanation: Foreign direct investment (FDI) is investment by an individual or enterprise from one country into a business or productive asset in another country, generally involving a lasting interest or significant influence in the enterprise.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does disinvestment always result in transfer of management control?

options.A: Yes, it always results in transfer of control
options.B: No, it may or may not result in transfer of management control
options.C: Yes, it always results in complete privatisation
options.D: No, it never results in transfer of control

questions.explanation: Disinvestment is the sale by the government of part or all of its equity in a public sector enterprise. It may or may not result in transfer of management control.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension of globalisation?

options.A: Economic

questions.explanation: The major dimensions are economic, political, technological, cultural, social and environmental globalisation. Feudal is not a dimension of globalisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of the factory system?

options.A: Workers, machines and materials brought together in a central workplace

questions.explanation: The factory system is a mode of production in which workers, machines and materials are brought together in a central workplace under organised management to produce goods, usually on a large scale.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What can deindustrialisation result from?

options.A: Structural change

questions.explanation: Deindustrialisation can result from structural change, automation, global competition, policy changes or industrial decline.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of the organised sector?

options.A: Enterprises operating within formal legal and regulatory frameworks

questions.explanation: The organised sector generally consists of enterprises and employment operating within formal legal and regulatory frameworks, with required records and applicable labour protections.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the informal sector?

options.A: Limited formal registration

questions.explanation: The unorganised or informal sector includes economic activities and workers with varying degrees of limited formal registration, job security, written contracts and social protection.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What do trade unions protect?

options.A: Wages and working conditions

questions.explanation: A trade union is an organisation of workers formed to protect and advance their employment-related interests, including wages, working conditions, rights and collective bargaining.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does sustainable industrialisation seek to improve?

options.A: Resource efficiency

questions.explanation: Sustainable industrialisation seeks to expand productive industrial activity while improving resource efficiency, worker safety and environmental performance and reducing pollution and emissions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following contributes to urbanisation?

options.A: Reclassification of settlements

questions.explanation: Rural-to-urban migration, natural population growth in urban settlements, industrialisation, expansion of services, education, employment opportunities, infrastructure development and reclassification of settlements contribute to urbanisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a pull factor of migration?

options.A: Jobs and higher wages

questions.explanation: Pull factors are conditions that attract people to a destination, such as jobs, higher wages, education, healthcare, transport, safety and better access to services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a push factor of migration?

options.A: Unemployment and low income

questions.explanation: Push factors are conditions that encourage people to leave a place, such as unemployment, low income, landlessness, drought, conflict, poor services or lack of educational opportunities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the deficiencies associated with slums?

options.A: Inadequate housing
options.B: Lack of safe water and sanitation

questions.explanation: A slum is a densely populated urban settlement or area characterised by inadequate housing and deficiencies in basic services such as safe water, sanitation, drainage, roads or secure tenure.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of urban poverty?

options.A: Insecure work

questions.explanation: Urban poverty is deprivation among people living in towns and cities, including inadequate income, insecure work, poor housing, limited access to essential services and vulnerability to high living costs.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution deals with municipalities?

options.A: Part IXA

questions.explanation: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, inserted Part IXA concerning municipalities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with municipalities?

options.A: Twelfth Schedule

questions.explanation: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, inserted the Twelfth Schedule concerning municipalities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with Panchayats?

options.A: Eleventh Schedule

questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, inserted the Eleventh Schedule relating to Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What population threshold defines a metropolitan area under Article 243P(c)?

options.A: Ten lakh or more

questions.explanation: Article 243P(c) defines a metropolitan area as an area with a population of ten lakh or more.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between a census town and a statutory town?

options.A: A census town meets demographic and occupational criteria but may not have an urban local body, while a statutory town has an urban local body
options.C: A statutory town has no local body
options.D: A census town always has a municipal corporation

questions.explanation: A census town is a settlement that meets the Census of India's specified demographic and occupational criteria for an urban area but is not necessarily governed as a statutory municipality. A statutory town is a place with an urban local body such as a municipality, municipal corporation, cantonment board or notified town area committee.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does urban sprawl refer to?

options.A: The outward, often low-density and poorly coordinated expansion of urban development into surrounding rural or peri-urban areas

questions.explanation: Urban sprawl is the outward, often low-density and poorly coordinated expansion of urban development into surrounding rural or peri-urban areas.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of horizontal mobility?

options.A: A teacher moving to a similar teaching post in another institution
options.B: A person being promoted to principal
options.C: A person losing their job and moving to a lower status
options.D: A child attaining a higher occupation than their parents

questions.explanation: Horizontal mobility is movement from one social position to another at broadly the same level of social status, such as a teacher moving to a similar teaching post in another institution.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of upward social mobility?

options.A: A person from a low-income background obtains a professional qualification and enters a substantially higher-paid occupation
options.B: A person loses a stable high-income occupation
options.C: A teacher moves to a similar teaching post
options.D: A person remains in the same occupation as their parents

questions.explanation: Upward mobility is movement to a higher social position, for example when a person from a low-income background obtains a professional qualification and enters a substantially higher-paid occupation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of downward social mobility?

options.A: A person loses a stable high-income occupation and experiences a major decline in income and status
options.B: A person from a low-income background enters a higher-paid occupation
options.C: A teacher moves to a similar teaching post
options.D: A person attains a higher occupation than their parents

questions.explanation: Downward mobility is movement to a lower social position, for example when a person loses a stable high-income occupation and experiences a major decline in income and status.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of intergenerational mobility?

options.A: A child's occupational position differing from that of their parents
options.B: A person changing occupation during their own lifetime
options.C: A teacher moving to a similar post
options.D: A person remaining in the same occupation as their parents

questions.explanation: Intergenerational mobility is a change in social or economic position between one generation and the next, such as a child's occupational position differing from that of their parents.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of intragenerational mobility?

options.A: A person changing occupation during their own lifetime
options.B: A child's occupation differing from that of their parents
options.C: A teacher moving to a similar post
options.D: A person remaining in the same occupation throughout their life

questions.explanation: Intragenerational mobility is a change in an individual's social or economic position during that person's own lifetime.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is an example of structural mobility?

options.A: Broad changes in the economy creating new occupational positions that enable many people to move between class categories
options.B: A person changing jobs at the same level
options.C: A child attaining a higher occupation than their parents

questions.explanation: Structural mobility occurs when broad changes in the economy or social structure alter the number or distribution of positions, enabling or requiring many people to move between occupational or class categories.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor that promotes social mobility?

options.A: Education

questions.explanation: Caste discrimination is a barrier to social mobility, not a factor that promotes it. Education, economic growth, industrialisation, urbanisation, migration, access to capital and land, fair recruitment, anti-discrimination measures and public welfare policies can promote mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a barrier to social mobility?

options.A: Gender inequality

questions.explanation: Poverty, unequal education, caste discrimination, gender inequality, disability-related barriers, inherited wealth disparities, regional inequality, lack of networks and insecure employment can restrict mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does education always guarantee upward social mobility?

options.A: Yes, education always guarantees upward mobility
options.B: No, its effect depends on educational quality, affordability, labour-market opportunities and the removal of discrimination
options.D: No, education has no effect on mobility

questions.explanation: Education can provide qualifications, skills and access to occupations that improve income and status. Its effect depends on educational quality, affordability, labour-market opportunities and the removal of discrimination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What can limit the mobility opportunities created by urbanisation?

options.A: High living costs
options.C: Unequal access to housing and services

questions.explanation: Urbanisation can create access to diverse occupations, education, markets and social networks, supporting mobility. However, high living costs, informal employment and unequal access to housing and services can limit these opportunities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What determines the extent of mobility created by industrialisation?

options.A: Labour conditions

questions.explanation: Industrialisation can create new occupations, wage employment, technical skills and professional opportunities, allowing some people to move beyond inherited occupations. The extent of mobility depends on labour conditions, education and access to jobs.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Is caste identity simply interchangeable with class position?

options.A: Yes, caste and class are the same
options.B: No, caste identity is not simply interchangeable with class position
options.D: No, caste has no relation to social position

questions.explanation: Caste mobility may occur through economic change, political mobilisation, education, social reform and changes in local power relations, but caste identity is not simply interchangeable with class position.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does social mobility automatically remove unequal access to wealth, power, education, social networks or opportunities?

options.A: Yes, mobility eliminates all inequality
options.B: No, structural reforms may also be needed to address unequal access
options.D: No, mobility has no effect on inequality

questions.explanation: Mobility can change the position of individuals or groups, but it does not automatically remove unequal access to wealth, power, education, social networks or opportunities. Structural reforms may also be needed.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does absolute mobility measure?

options.A: Whether people have moved to different positions compared with their parents or earlier generations
options.B: The strength of the relationship between origins and destinations
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement due to structural changes only

questions.explanation: Absolute mobility measures whether people have moved to different positions compared with their parents or earlier generations, often due to changes in the occupational structure.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does relative mobility measure?

options.A: The strength of the relationship between people's origins and destinations, or their chances of reaching positions compared with others
options.B: Whether people have moved to different positions compared with their parents
options.C: Movement at the same level of social status
options.D: Movement due to structural changes only

questions.explanation: Relative mobility measures the strength of the relationship between people's origins and destinations, or their chances of reaching positions compared with others.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are important conditions for social mobility to support social justice in a democratic society?

options.A: Equal opportunity

questions.explanation: Social mobility can widen opportunities, reduce inherited disadvantage, support social justice and allow people to participate more fully in economic and public life. Equal opportunity and protection against discrimination are important conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can social change be gradual or rapid?

options.A: No, it is always gradual
options.C: Yes, it can be gradual or rapid, planned or unplanned

questions.explanation: Social change is a continuing transformation in social relationships, institutions, values, norms and structures. It can be gradual or rapid, planned or unplanned, and may create both opportunities and inequalities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does social change transform?

options.A: Social relationships

questions.explanation: Social change is a continuing transformation in social relationships, institutions, values, norms and structures.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of modernisation related to political participation?

options.A: Wider political participation

questions.explanation: Major features of modernisation include wider political participation along with scientific temper, technological development, industrial and service-sector expansion, urban growth, literacy and education, occupational specialisation, bureaucratic organisation, mass communication, mobility and individual achievement.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of modernisation related to social organisation?

options.A: Bureaucratic organisation

questions.explanation: Modernisation features include occupational specialisation, bureaucratic organisation, mass communication, mobility and individual achievement.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following institutions was expanded by British rule in India?

options.A: Railways

questions.explanation: British rule introduced or expanded Western-style administrative, legal and educational institutions, railways, postal and telegraph systems, modern military and bureaucratic structures, and English-language education.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following political ideas spread through Western education in India?

options.A: Liberal thought

questions.explanation: Western education contributed to the spread of modern sciences, new forms of professional training, political ideas, liberal and constitutional thought, print culture and reform debates.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following contributed to the spread of print culture in colonial India?

options.A: Western education

questions.explanation: Western education contributed to the spread of modern sciences, new forms of professional training, political ideas, liberal and constitutional thought, print culture and reform debates.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of institutional differentiation?

options.A: Government, law, education and science developing their own specialised functions rather than being directly governed by religious authorities
options.B: Religious authorities controlling all public institutions
options.C: The establishment of a state religion
options.D: The merging of religious and secular institutions

questions.explanation: Institutional differentiation is the process through which institutions such as government, law, education, science and the economy develop their own specialised functions rather than being directly governed by religious authorities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following can secularisation support in modern society?

options.A: Specialised public institutions
options.C: Equal civic participation across religious communities

questions.explanation: Secularisation can support specialised public institutions, evidence-based policy and equal civic participation across religious communities. Its effects differ according to social history and political institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution protect minority cultural and educational rights?

options.A: Articles 29 and 30

questions.explanation: The original Constitution contained important protections for freedom of conscience and religion, including Articles 25 to 28, as well as equality and minority cultural and educational rights under Articles 29 and 30.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Does Article 27 prevent the State from levying taxes for the promotion of any particular religion?

options.A: Yes, it protects persons from being compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion of any particular religion
options.B: No, it allows taxes for promoting any religion
options.D: No, it has no relation to religion

questions.explanation: Article 27 protects persons from being compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 28 regulate?

options.A: Religious instruction or worship in educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 28 regulates religious instruction or worship in educational institutions and provides protections concerning participation or attendance in specified circumstances.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following describes communalism?

options.A: Politicisation of religious identity in ways that may create hostility or division between communities
options.B: Changes in the social authority and institutional role of religion
options.C: The separation of religion from the State

questions.explanation: Communalism politicises religious identity in ways that may create hostility or division between communities. Secularisation concerns changes in the social authority and institutional role of religion; the concepts describe different phenomena.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the full form of WTO?

options.A: World Trade Organization

questions.explanation: WTO stands for World Trade Organization.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the full form of IMF?

options.A: International Monetary Fund

questions.explanation: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which two institutions commonly constitute the 'World Bank'?

options.A: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association
options.C: The Asian Development Bank and the African Development Bank
options.D: The RBI and the World Trade Organization

questions.explanation: The term 'World Bank' commonly refers to the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does information technology enable global supply-chain coordination?

options.A: Yes, it enables rapid communication, digital trade, remote work and global supply-chain coordination
options.B: No, it only enables local communication
options.C: No, it has no role in trade
options.D: Yes, but only for government organisations

questions.explanation: Information technology enables rapid communication, digital trade, remote work, global supply-chain coordination, online education, financial services and cross-border exchange of information.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Is globalisation a multidirectional process involving many countries and cultures?

options.A: No, it is only a one-way flow from the West to other countries
options.B: Yes, globalisation involves multidirectional cross-border flows among many countries and cultures
options.C: No, it only involves economic flows
options.D: Yes, but only between developed countries

questions.explanation: Globalisation involves multidirectional cross-border flows among many countries and cultures. Westernisation specifically refers to influence from Western societies and institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a factor promoting industrialisation?

options.A: Entrepreneurship

questions.explanation: Capital, raw materials, energy, labour, technology, transport, markets, infrastructure, entrepreneurship, government policy, financial institutions and stable institutions can promote industrialisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin in the eighteenth century?

options.A: Britain

questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution refers to the major transformation in production that began in Britain in the eighteenth century and spread to other regions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What did the Industrial Revolution involve?

options.A: Mechanisation
options.C: New energy sources and changes in transport and labour

questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution involved mechanisation, factory systems, new energy sources and changes in transport and labour.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does industrialisation only occur through manufacturing growth?

options.A: Yes, only through manufacturing
options.B: No, it can also involve other industrial activities and occupational transformation
options.D: No, industrialisation is unrelated to manufacturing

questions.explanation: Industrialisation is the process through which an economy develops and expands manufacturing and other industrial activities, often accompanied by mechanisation, technological change, factory production, capital investment and occupational transformation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of occupational transformation due to industrialisation?

options.A: Movement from agricultural work to factory wage employment
options.B: Continued reliance on subsistence agriculture only

questions.explanation: Industrialisation expands wage labour and can create an industrial working class whose members depend on wages and work in factories, mines, construction, transport and related sectors.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of natural population growth in urbanisation?

options.A: It contributes to the growth of urban populations
options.B: It has no role in urbanisation

questions.explanation: Natural population growth in urban settlements is one of the factors contributing to urbanisation, along with rural-to-urban migration, industrialisation, expansion of services, education, employment opportunities, infrastructure development and reclassification of settlements.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does urbanisation only occur through migration?

options.A: Yes, only through migration
options.B: No, it can also occur through natural population growth, industrialisation, expansion of services and reclassification of settlements

questions.explanation: Rural-to-urban migration, natural population growth in urban settlements, industrialisation, expansion of services, education, employment opportunities, infrastructure development and reclassification of settlements contribute to urbanisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between urbanisation and family patterns?

options.A: Urbanisation changes family patterns, occupations, social networks, lifestyles, gender roles, consumption and political participation
options.B: Urbanisation has no effect on family patterns
options.D: Urbanisation preserves all traditional family patterns

questions.explanation: Urbanisation changes family patterns, occupations, social networks, lifestyles, gender roles, consumption, political participation and access to education and services. It can create opportunities as well as new inequalities and pressures.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Is social mobility the same as physical migration?

options.A: Yes, they are the same
options.B: No, social mobility refers to movement between social positions, while migration refers to physical movement between places
options.C: Yes, both refer to movement between places
options.D: No, social mobility refers to physical movement

questions.explanation: Social mobility is the movement of individuals or groups from one social position or status to another within a system of social stratification. Migration is the physical movement of people between places.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can social mobility involve changes to the hierarchy itself?

options.A: No, social mobility only involves movement within a fixed hierarchy
options.B: Yes, social mobility can describe movement between positions within the hierarchy or changes to the hierarchy itself
options.D: Yes, but only for individuals, not groups

questions.explanation: Social stratification is the structured ranking of groups in society. Social mobility describes movement between positions within that hierarchy or changes to the hierarchy itself.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between social stratification and social mobility?

options.A: Social stratification is the structured ranking of groups, and social mobility describes movement within or changes to that hierarchy
options.C: Social mobility is the ranking of groups
options.D: Social stratification describes movement between positions

questions.explanation: Social stratification is the structured ranking of groups in society. Social mobility describes movement between positions within that hierarchy or changes to the hierarchy itself.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of achieved status?

options.A: Becoming a doctor through education and qualification
options.B: Being born into a particular caste

questions.explanation: Achieved status is acquired through a person's actions, qualifications or accomplishments, such as becoming a doctor through education and qualification.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of ascribed status?

options.A: Being born into a particular caste or inheriting a social position

questions.explanation: Ascribed status is assigned at birth or independently of individual choice, such as age or inherited social position in many social systems.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does unequal starting conditions affect how fairly merit is assessed in a meritocracy?

options.A: No, merit is always assessed fairly
options.B: Yes, unequal starting conditions can affect how fairly merit is assessed
options.C: No, starting conditions have no effect
options.D: Yes, but only in developed countries

questions.explanation: Meritocracy is an ideal system in which positions and rewards are allocated according to ability, achievement and performance. In practice, unequal starting conditions can affect how fairly merit is assessed.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does globalisation only involve economic flows?

options.A: Yes, it only involves economic flows
options.B: No, it involves economic, political, technological, cultural, social and environmental dimensions
options.C: Yes, it only involves cultural flows
options.D: No, it only involves political flows

questions.explanation: Globalisation is the growing interconnectedness and interdependence of countries, societies and economies through trade, investment, technology, migration, communication, culture and the movement of information and ideas. The major dimensions are economic, political, technological, cultural, social and environmental.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can globalisation lead to cultural homogenisation?

options.A: No, globalisation always preserves local cultures
options.B: Yes, globalisation can lead to cultural homogenisation, where cultural practices become more similar across societies
options.D: Yes, but only in developed countries

questions.explanation: Cultural homogenisation is the tendency for cultural practices, products or lifestyles to become more similar across societies, sometimes at the expense of local distinctiveness. It is one of the challenges of globalisation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can globalisation lead to cultural hybridisation?

options.A: No, globalisation only destroys local cultures
options.B: Yes, globalisation can lead to cultural hybridisation through the blending and adaptation of elements from different cultures
options.D: Yes, but only in developed countries

questions.explanation: Cultural hybridisation is the creation of new cultural forms through the blending and adaptation of elements from different cultures. Globalisation can facilitate this process.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a source of financial volatility associated with globalisation?

options.A: Dependence on global markets

questions.explanation: Challenges of globalisation can include financial volatility and vulnerability to international crises due to dependence on global markets and cross-border financial flows.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How does globalisation affect small producers?

options.A: It can create pressure on small producers due to competition from larger global firms
options.B: It always benefits small producers equally
options.C: It has no effect on small producers

questions.explanation: Challenges of globalisation can include pressure on small producers due to increased competition, unequal gains and dependence on global markets.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a challenge of modernisation related to inequality?

options.A: Uneven distribution of development

questions.explanation: Possible challenges of modernisation include environmental degradation, consumerism, inequality, cultural dislocation, weakening of some traditional support networks, job displacement, digital exclusion and uneven distribution of development.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a challenge of modernisation related to culture?

options.A: Cultural dislocation
options.B: Weakening of some traditional support networks

questions.explanation: Possible challenges of modernisation include environmental degradation, consumerism, inequality, cultural dislocation, weakening of some traditional support networks, job displacement, digital exclusion and uneven distribution of development.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does Westernisation necessarily weaken all local practices?

options.A: Yes, it always weakens all local practices
options.B: No, Westernisation may involve selective adoption and adaptation, and Indian society has combined Western influences with indigenous traditions
options.C: Yes, local practices are completely eliminated
options.D: No, Westernisation has no effect on local practices

questions.explanation: Westernisation may involve selective adoption, adaptation or rejection of particular practices. Indian society has combined Western influences with indigenous traditions and institutions in varied ways. Criticisms include weakening of some local practices, but not all.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 25 guarantee regarding religion?

options.A: Freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion
options.B: The right to establish a state religion
options.C: The right to compel others to follow a religion
options.D: The right to tax for religious promotion

questions.explanation: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 26 protect regarding religious denominations?

options.A: The right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage religious affairs, and own and administer property
options.B: The right to establish a state religion
options.C: The right to compel others to follow a religion
options.D: The right to tax for religious promotion

questions.explanation: Article 26 protects the rights of religious denominations or sections thereof to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage religious affairs, and own and administer property in accordance with law, subject to public order, morality and health.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 27 protect against?

options.A: Being compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion of any particular religion

questions.explanation: Article 27 protects persons from being compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 28 regulate?

options.A: Religious instruction or worship in educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 28 regulates religious instruction or worship in educational institutions and provides protections concerning participation or attendance in specified circumstances.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does secularisation require the complete separation of religion from all social life?

options.A: Yes, religion must be completely removed from social life
options.B: No, secularisation involves changes in the influence and role of religion in certain institutions, but religion may remain important in personal life and community identity
options.C: Yes, religion must be eliminated entirely
options.D: No, secularisation has no effect on religion

questions.explanation: Secularisation is a process in which social institutions, public authority, law, education or other areas of social life become less directly controlled by religious institutions or religious explanations. Religion may remain important in personal life, community identity, public debate and politics.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does institutional differentiation in secularisation refer to?

options.A: Institutions such as government, law, education, science and the economy developing their own specialised functions rather than being directly governed by religious authorities
options.B: The merging of religious and secular institutions
options.C: The establishment of a state religion

questions.explanation: Institutional differentiation is the process through which institutions such as government, law, education, science and the economy develop their own specialised functions rather than being directly governed by religious authorities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of political globalisation?

options.A: The growing influence of international organisations, treaties and transnational movements on national policy
options.B: The spread of cultural products across borders
options.C: The integration of national economies through trade
options.D: The worldwide spread of digital networks

questions.explanation: Political globalisation refers to the growing influence of international organisations, treaties, transnational movements and cross-border issues on national policy and governance.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of technological globalisation?

options.A: The worldwide spread and interconnection of technologies, digital networks, scientific knowledge and communication systems
options.B: The spread of cultural products across borders
options.C: The integration of national economies through trade
options.D: The influence of international organisations on national policy

questions.explanation: Technological globalisation refers to the worldwide spread and interconnection of technologies, digital networks, scientific knowledge and communication systems.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of economic globalisation?

options.A: The increasing integration of national economies through international trade, foreign investment and financial flows
options.B: The spread of cultural products across borders
options.C: The influence of international organisations on national policy
options.D: The worldwide spread of digital networks

questions.explanation: Economic globalisation is the increasing integration of national economies through international trade, foreign investment, global production networks, financial flows and movement of services and technology.
